workshopTitle: Google Antigravity workshop by T M Saravanan

prompts.title: Module 1: Floating Header & Terminal Intro
prompts.content:
Act as a creative UI/UX designer and staff frontend engineer. Using Antigravity IDE, build the hero screen and navigation bar for my personal developer portfolio using React and Tailwind CSS.

- Theme & Aesthetic: 'Cyber-Emerald / High-Tech Monolith' (Avoid generic blue gradients). Use an ultra-deep matte carbon background (#0d1117) with subtle neon emerald (#10b981) and radioactive lime (#84cc16) micro-accents.
- Interactive Ambient Background: An interactive HTML5 canvas showing an animated matrix-dot grid that slightly ripples or shifts perspective when the mouse hovers over it.
- Navigation: Sleek floating navbar styled like an IDE status bar with a soft glassmorphism blur (backdrop-blur-md), displaying my logo and links: 'Overview', 'Artifacts', 'Capabilities', and 'Signal'.
- Hero Content:
  - Status Pill: An animated radar-blinking dot: '🟢 Agent Online // Ready for Deployment'
  - Headline: 'Hi, I am [REPLACE: YOUR NAME] — Architecting Autonomous Code.'
  - Sub-headline: '[REPLACE: YOUR ROLE] specializing in full-stack interfaces, agentic systems, and high-performance applications.'
  - Action Buttons: Primary button 'Launch Artifacts' with a glowing emerald scanline hover effect, and a ghost button 'Read Docs'.
- Ensure the layout is responsive across desktop and mobile screens.
prompts.notes: In Antigravity IDE, hit the prompt input and swap [REPLACE: YOUR NAME] and [REPLACE: YOUR ROLE] with your info. Leave the hex codes as they are.
prompts.presenterTip: In Antigravity IDE, hit the prompt input and swap [REPLACE: YOUR NAME] and [REPLACE: YOUR ROLE] with your info. Leave the hex codes as they are.
prompts.whyItWorks: Replaces generic blue palettes with an ultra-tech emerald/carbon aesthetic suited for Antigravity IDE. It defines exact typography, interactive canvas requirements, and clear layout elements so the agent outputs working code immediately.
prompts.howNotToPrompt:
Example: 'Make an intro section for my portfolio in Antigravity IDE with cool tech colors and a nav bar.'
Why it fails: 'Cool tech colors' usually defaults right back to generic blue/purple neon, and missing layout specs results in broken button alignments.

prompts.title: Module 2: Interactive Mission Artifacts
prompts.content:
Keep the existing carbon and neon-emerald aesthetic. Directly beneath the Hero, add an 'Artifacts & Builds' showcase section.

- Layout: Responsive 3-column card grid.
- Visual & Interactive Card Physics:
  - Styled like cybernetic hardware panels: dark carbon backing, subtle 1px emerald border (border-emerald-500/20), and an interactive 3D perspective tilt that tracks mouse position.
  - On hover: The card casts an intense emerald corner flare, lifts slightly, and displays an animated scanline sweeping across the card background.
- Card Content:
  - Artifact 1: [REPLACE: Project One Name] — 2-sentence breakdown, tech stack badges (e.g., 'TypeScript', 'Antigravity API'), and actionable buttons: 'Inspect Code' and 'Live Preview'.
  - Artifact 2: [REPLACE: Project Two Name] — 2-sentence breakdown and tech stack badges.
  - Artifact 3: [REPLACE: Project Three Name] — 2-sentence breakdown and tech stack badges.
- Add an interactive category filter bar ('All', 'Autonomous Systems', 'Frontends') that updates the grid with a smooth fade-and-slide transition.
prompts.notes: Replace the 3 artifact names with your real projects or hackathon ideas. Once generated, move your cursor over each card to test the 3D tilt and scanline flare.
prompts.presenterTip: Replace the 3 artifact names with your real projects or hackathon ideas. Once generated, move your cursor over each card to test the 3D tilt and scanline flare.
prompts.whyItWorks: Enforces visual continuity so the agent doesn't rewrite existing styles. The 3D tilt and scanline hover effects give the cards a tactile, hardware-console feel without relying on clunky third-party libraries.
prompts.howNotToPrompt:
Example: 'Add 3 project cards that look like high-tech cards and tilt when I touch them.'
Why it fails: It lacks data structure and motion parameters, causing the agent to write buggy mouse-tracking code that stutters or miscalculates offsets.

prompts.title: Module 3: Neural Capabilities & Milestones
prompts.content:
Append an interactive 'Capabilities & Execution History' section below the artifacts, matching the cyber-emerald theme.

- Interactive Skill Matrix:
  - Render skills as interactive cybernetic tags (e.g., Python, Rust, Prompt Architecture, React, Agent Workflows, Tailwind CSS).
  - Micro-Interaction: Each tag has a faint pulse animation. Hovering over a tag triggers a rapid text-scramble/decoding glitch effect before settling on the clean word, accompanied by an emerald border glow.
- Deployment Log (Timeline):
  - Vertical circuit-trace timeline adjacent to the skill matrix, connected by an animated electric pulse running down the line.
  - 3 milestone nodes:
    - 2026: [REPLACE: Recent Milestone, e.g., Deployed AI Multi-Agent System]
    - 2025: [REPLACE: Previous Milestone, e.g., Senior Engineering Lead]
    - 2024: [REPLACE: Starting Milestone, e.g., Initiated Deep Tech Architecture]
- Keep animations GPU-accelerated and smooth.
prompts.notes: Customize the 3 milestone dates and achievements with your background. Hover over the skill tags to watch the hacker decode effect happen in real-time.
prompts.presenterTip: Customize the 3 milestone dates and achievements with your background. Hover over the skill tags to watch the hacker decode effect happen in real-time.
prompts.whyItWorks: The text-scramble/decoding glitch effect adds an authentic developer/hacker interaction that avoids generic bouncing badges. Specifying GPU acceleration keeps the Antigravity preview snappy and lightweight.
prompts.howNotToPrompt:
Example: 'Put my skills and a timeline on the page with hacker animations.'
Why it fails: 'Hacker animations' often makes the agent generate aggressive, unreadable green terminal spam that obscures text and slows down browser rendering.

prompts.title: Module 4: Signal Transmission & Reactive Canvas
prompts.content:
Finalize the portfolio by adding a 'Transmit Signal' contact console and overall interactive polish.

- Contact Console:
  - Header: 'Initiate Secure Transmission'
  - Subtext: 'Route a direct packet or proposal to my frequency.'
  - Form inputs: 'Callsign / Name', 'Return Signal / Email', and 'Encrypted Payload / Message'.
  - Interactive Action Button: 'Transmit Message'. On click, show an animated emerald progress bar inside the button that transitions to 'Packet Delivered! // 200 OK'.
  - Quick-connect buttons with magnetic pull hover effect: GitHub, LinkedIn, and Email ([REPLACE: yourname@example.com]).
- Global Cursor Magnet Effect: Add a subtle custom neon-ring cursor follower with a magnetic snap effect when hovering near buttons or cards.
- Footer: Minimal terminal line: '© 2026 [REPLACE: YOUR NAME] // Built with Antigravity IDE.'
- Deliver the complete, runnable code file with zero missing dependencies.
prompts.notes: Replace [REPLACE: yourname@example.com] and your footer name. After Antigravity finishes generating, test typing in the form and clicking 'Transmit' to see the status change!
prompts.presenterTip: Replace [REPLACE: yourname@example.com] and your footer name. After Antigravity finishes generating, test typing in the form and clicking 'Transmit' to see the status change!
prompts.whyItWorks: Gives the contact form unique sci-fi/terminal themed copy while maintaining functional UX feedback ('Packet Delivered! // 200 OK'). Requesting a complete runnable file ensures Antigravity IDE compiles the final app seamlessly.
prompts.howNotToPrompt:
Example: 'Finish the portfolio with a contact box and footer and make the mouse follow something.'
Why it fails: Vague cursor prompts often result in the AI completely disabling default clicks, making links and buttons impossible to activate.
